results.content: Interviewers are trained to betray no opinion about survey questions to minimize interviewer-related error that occurs when responses are influenced by respondent perception of what the interviewer indicates is an appropriate answer. Neutral administration of surveys requires the training of interviewers to not reveal their own opinions or preferences, either verbally or nonverbally, which could induce respondents to provide inaccurate answers in response to perceived interviewer preferences. Interviewers should avoid expressing personal opinions on the topics covered in the survey, as well as communicating any personal information that the respondent may use to infer the interviewer's opinions. Finally, social desirability (wanting to provide socially acceptable answers) and acquiescence response bias (the tendency to agree with perceived interviewers' opinions) can threaten the validity of the data. Acquiescence response bias occurs when respondents agree with statements from the questions that are spoken by the interviewer regardless of content and can lead to responses that merely reflect agreement with what the interviewer is reading rather than the respondent's own opinions.
